decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 10 headings are plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 400 links on this page open a file — 357 PDF, 43 PowerPoint — and say nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Give the cards the width their content needs
decisions.why: 1 row holds two cards of very different weight in equal halves, and cards in a row are the same height — so the short one is stretched and the difference shows as empty space. 323.2× — 15837 characters beside 49. Only the column widths change.

decisions.label: Let a lone card use the full width
decisions.why: 1 row holds a single card in a part-width column, so it takes a third or a half of the page and the rest is blank. A row of one is not a grid.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 3 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Let a colon do its own work
decisions.why: A colon marks the words before it as a term and the words after it as what the term means. Here 21 list items open with a term set in the same weight as its own explanation, so the list cannot be scanned. 2 links sit immediately in front of a colon, where the chevron lands between the term and the punctuation that belongs to it. 2 format tags stand between a title and its description and move to the end of the row. No word changes and nothing is removed.

decisions.label: Let a long table be searched
decisions.why: 1 table runs to fifteen rows or more, so finding one row means reading every row. The theme already loads the search behaviour on every page and switches it on for any table marked this way — 26 tables across the site already are, including the contact directory. It adds a search box and a "show 25 entries" menu above the table, makes the column headings sortable, and pages below twenty-five rows at a time — which leaves all but the longest tables whole. Nothing is reordered and nothing changes until someone types.
